item.title: Electric-Field-Driven Optical Tunability in MoSe₂/WSe₂ van der Waals Type-II Heterostructures: Valley-Selective Quantum Confined Stark Effect
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Amit Kumar Sinha, A. M. Khan
This study investigates how an applied electric field affects light-matter interactions differently in the two momentum valleys (K and K′) of MoSe₂/WSe₂ van der Waals heterostructures — a phenomenon termed valley-selective quantum confined Stark effect (QCSE). A three-tier theoretical framework was built combining density functional theory for band parameters, an envelope-function formalism for carrier wavefunctions, and a massive Dirac fermion Hamiltonian that separately accounts for spin-orbit coupling in each layer. This allowed independent computation of how exciton energy, oscillator strength, and radiative lifetime evolve in each valley as a function of electric field (0–200 kV/cm) and bilayer twist angle (0°–60°). item.title: Impact of geomagnetic storm intensity on thermospheric density and orbital decay of LEO satellites: a G1–G5 per-event analysis
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Jeong-Heon Kim, Giwoong Eom, Young-Sil Kwak, Tae-Yong Yang, Hwanil Huh
Geomagnetic storms enhance thermospheric density and increase atmospheric drag on low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites, accelerating their orbital decay, as illustrated by the loss of 38 Starlink satellites following the modest February 2022 storm. item.title: Analysis of Network Classification and Optimization Based on Comprehensive Evaluation of Public Transportation Network – A Case Study of Guangzhou
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 caixia li, Cong Cong, Hunan Deng, Jiachao Chen, Junhui Li
Urban bus networks in many megacities face simultaneous challenges of declining ridership, structural inefficiencies, and spatial inequity, yet existing evaluation frameworks rarely integrate topological, functional, and equity dimensions within a coherent analytical structure. This paper proposes a novel "structure–function–equity" evaluation framework that combines six topological indicators (network density, coverage rate, stop coverage, route length, repetition coefficient, and non-linear coefficient) with five functional indicators (supply index, population coverage, Gini coefficient, passenger flow, and metro overlap coefficient). item.title: Plug-and-play single-photon source can work at room temperature
item.description:
📚 Physics News
The Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS) has developed a room-temperature single-photon source built into a compact 19-inch rack-mounted device that operates without cryogenic cooling. Designed as a plug-and-play system that works as soon as it is powered on, the device moves quantum light source technology beyond the laboratory and closer to practical, onsite use.

item.title: Ultrafast scanning tunneling microscopy reaches the quantum mechanical space-time limit for the first time
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle describes one of the most intriguing features of quantum physics: certain pairs of physical quantities describing a particle, such as position and momentum, cannot simultaneously be determined with arbitrary precision—not because of imprecise measuring instruments, but because nature forbids it. Between position and time, however, there is no Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

item.title: AlGaN/GaN heterojunction field effect transistor structure integrated photoelectrode probe with optical artifact suppression function
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Xin Cao, Yanyuan Ding, Xi'en Yang, Wenbo Zhao, Xiaodong Li, Ye Wen 等11位作者
The integrated photoelectrode probe capable of simultaneously stimulating neurons with light and collecting electrophysiological signals is the core device of optogenetics. In this paper, AlGaN/GaN heterojunction field-effect transistors (HFETs) are used instead of the traditional metal microelectrode to prepare brain neural probe, and then bonded with the LED photoelectrode probe to form an integrated photoelectrode probe. The AlGaN/GaN HFET structure brain neural probe has high sensitivity and biocompatibility, which can effectively improve the quality of neuronal signal acquisition.
